2608.27135.title: Said Aloud, Read Different: Cross-Modal Instability in Multimodal Models
2608.27135.paper_summary: Multimodal foundation models are increasingly used in speech-first assistants that must interpret spoken queries and produce visually grounded decisions. Yet it remains unclear whether semantically equivalent queries yield consistent judgments across modality (text vs. speech) and language (English vs. Arabic). We introduce a speech-augmented visually grounded contrastive triplet benchmark spanning 10,150 culturally grounded images from 18 MENA countries, where each image is paired with one supported statement and two plausible but unsupported alternatives. We define contrastive instability as the conditional rate at which a model fails to resolve all statements within a triplet, isolating fragmented reasoning from complete failure. Evaluating recent multimodal models under text and speech in English and Arabic, we find that modality and language shifts introduce substantial triplet-level inconsistencies that are not fully captured by aggregate accuracy, with speech amplifying partial failures. We make the benchmark publicly available to the community.
2608.27135.paper_summary_zh: 多模態基礎模型在語音優先的助手中越來越常被使用，這些助手必須解釋口語查詢並產生視覺上有根據的決策。<lb/>然而，目前尚不清楚語義等價的查詢是否在不同模態（文本與語音）和語言（英語與阿拉伯語）之間產生一致的判斷。<lb/>我們引入了一個語音增強的視覺基礎對比三元組基準，涵蓋來自18個中東和北非國家的10,150張文化根植的圖像，其中每張圖像都配有一個支持的陳述和兩個合理但不支持的替代選項。<lb/>我們將對比不穩定性定義為模型在三元組中無法解決所有陳述的條件比率，將片段推理與完全失敗隔離開來。<lb/>在英語和阿拉伯語的文本和語音下評估近期的多模態模型時，我們發現模態和語言的轉變引入了相當大的三元組級不一致性，這些不一致性並未被總體準確率充分捕捉，並且語音放大了部分失敗。<lb/>我們將該基準公開提供給社群。
